title: The Playlist of Lake Minnow
premise: Wendell Joubert, seventeen and parentified, has survived seven years at Lake Minnow High by being forgettable — until the school's legendary ghost begins leaving notes in ink that shifts color, addressed to them by a name they buried long ago. The notes demand Wendell enter two competitions: the school's meaningless trivia championship and the hidden contest the ghost actually runs, where students wager secrets for survival. As Wendell's carefully managed life frays — siblings noticing, mom working double shifts, prom looming as social execution — they discover the ghost is a former student who made the same bargain decades ago and never escaped it. To break the cycle, Wendell must win both championships: the one that doesn't matter to save face, and the one that does to free the ghost, even if winning means surrendering the invisibility that kept their family safe.
about_author: Lena Dravenmoor grew up in a fading mill town where every high school had its own ghost story, and she never stopped wondering who the ghosts used to be. She writes young adult fiction about kids who carry too much, too early, and the strange magic that finds them anyway.

chapters.title: Invisible Ink
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. A routine night of microwaving dinners and checking homework ends with a note tucked into their locker: 'Hello again, Wren.' The name no one has used since fourth grade, written in ink that shimmers blue then vanishes. Wendell burns it and tells no one, but can't stop shaking. Emotional beat: dread wrapped in a flicker of being seen.

chapters.title: The Rules of Being Careful
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. We meet the Joubert household: mom's night shifts, little sister Odile's scraped knees, brother Theo's silent hunger. Wendell maps their invisibility strategy like a survival manual. Then a second note appears inside their textbook, listing things only Wendell could know. Emotional beat: the cost of vigilance, and the terror of being known.

chapters.title: Everyone Knows About the Ghost
chapters.summary: Dual POV with best friend Priya. In the library stacks, Priya recounts the legend: a student who vanished in 1987 after losing something at prom. Wendell realizes the notes match the anniversary dates. When a third note names the trivia championship, Wendell refuses — until the note predicts Odile's fall from the monkey bars an hour before it happens. Emotional beat: refusal cracking into obligation.

chapters.title: Trivia Night for People With Better Things to Do
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Dragged into the qualifying round by Priya, Wendell discovers they know everything — years of listening, memorizing, watching. They qualify easily and hate how good it feels. That night, the ghost's note congratulates them and mentions 'the other championship.' Emotional beat: reluctant pride curdling into suspicion that they're being groomed.

chapters.title: What Marcus Knew
chapters.summary: Marcus Hale's POV, the golden boy who lost his scholarship secret last semester. He warns Wendell about the second contest: students trade secrets to the ghost for favors, and the debts compound. Marcus shows his own shifting-ink scar on his wrist. Emotional beat: horror of complicity; power revealed as a trap dressed as rescue.

chapters.title: The Championship That Doesn't Matter
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The trivia final collides with mom's missed rent notice. Wendell wins spectacularly, becoming briefly visible — and immediately targeted: mocked online, invited to parties as a joke. The ghost's note says visibility was always the price of entry. Emotional beat: victory that feels like exposure; belonging offered on humiliating terms.

chapters.title: Prom Is a Weapon
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Prom approaches as social battlefield. Wendell, now half-visible, gets asked out as a dare and nearly declines everything — including the ghost's summons. Odile finds one of the notes and reads it aloud. Wendell finally confesses everything to their siblings, expecting collapse, receiving instead fierce, clumsy solidarity. Emotional beat: the family Wendell protected chooses to protect them back.

chapters.title: The Second Championship
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Following the notes' trail into the school's sealed 1987 wing, Wendell enters the ghost's true contest: a night of riddles built from the vanished student's life. Wendell learns her name — Renata — and that she traded her future to save her siblings, then couldn't pay the final debt. Emotional beat: recognition across decades; the ghost is a mirror.

chapters.title: The Debt
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV, climax. The final challenge demands Wendell surrender their own name — become the next keeper, invisible forever, so Renata can go free. On prom night, in front of the whole school, Wendell instead offers what the ghost truly lacks: not a replacement, but a witness. They speak Renata's story aloud, and the ink-notes blaze through the gym as the debt transforms rather than transfers. Emotional beat: sacrifice refused in favor of truth; power broken by being shared.

chapters.title: Encore
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV, weeks later. Renata is gone; the wing stands empty and warm. Wendell is still visible — awkwardly, imperfectly — running an after-school homework table with Theo and Odile underfoot, dating the boy who asked sincerely the second time. A last note appears, plain black ink, unsigned: 'Thank you, Wren.' Emotional beat: quiet resolution; belonging earned, survival redefined as living, not hiding.
